title: NCR 5386 SCSI protocol controller

sources.document: NCR Microelectronics Division SCSI Engineering Notebook, Rev. 2, October 1985
sources.pages: 41 (NCR 5386 48-pin DIP pinout); 4-5 (differences from the 5385E: pin and software compatible superset, pass-parity on pin 14)

sources.document: NCR 5385E SCSI Protocol Controller Data Sheet, May 1985
sources.familyUsed: NCR 5385E - the notebook states the 5386 is pin compatible with it; pin names and numbers checked against the 5386 pinout

pins.name: D2
pins.text: microprocessor data bus bit 2, active high, bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state)

pins.name: D1
pins.text: microprocessor data bus bit 1, active high, bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state)

pins.name: D0
pins.text: microprocessor data bus bit 0, active high, bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state)

pins.name: RESET
pins.text: high forces the chip into reset: current operations end, internal storage is cleared and self-diagnostics run

pins.name: ATN
pins.text: INITIATOR ROLE: asserted when the microprocessor asks for attention or a received byte has a parity error. TARGET ROLE: input showing the SCSI ATN signal. bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state)

pins.name: IGS
pins.text: initiator group select: high when the chip works as initiator; enables the external ATN and ACK drivers

pins.name: I_O
pins.text: I/O. INITIATOR ROLE: input showing the bus phase. TARGET ROLE: driven to show the bus phase. bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state)

pins.name: C_D
pins.text: C/D. INITIATOR ROLE: input showing the bus phase. TARGET ROLE: driven to show the bus phase. bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state)

pins.name: MSG
pins.text: INITIATOR ROLE: input showing the bus phase. TARGET ROLE: driven to show the bus phase. bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state)

pins.name: ACK
pins.text: INITIATOR ROLE: asserted in answer to REQ for a byte transfer. TARGET ROLE: input answering REQ. bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state)

pins.name: REQ
pins.text: INITIATOR ROLE: input: the target asks for a byte transfer. TARGET ROLE: asserted to ask for a byte transfer. bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state)

pins.name: ID2
pins.text: SCSI ID bit 2 of the chip, active low; pull-up needed only when wired to a switch or strap

pins.name: ID1
pins.text: SCSI ID bit 1, active low

pins.name: ID0
pins.text: SCSI ID bit 0, active low. On the 5386 in pass-parity mode this pin is the data bus parity DP and pins 12-13 are unused (NCR SCSI Engineering Notebook)

pins.name: ARB
pins.text: arbitration phase: high lets external circuits put the ID bit on the SCSI bus

pins.name: CLK
pins.text: symmetrical square wave that makes the internal timing; at most 10 MHz

pins.name: BSYIN
pins.text: high tells the chip the SCSI BSY signal is active

pins.name: SELIN
pins.text: high tells the chip the SCSI SEL signal is active

pins.name: INT
pins.text: interrupt to the microprocessor; set high on a request, cleared by reset or by reading the Interrupt Register

pins.name: SBEN
pins.text: SCSI data bus enable: low enables the external SCSI data bus drivers

pins.name: CS
pins.text: chip select: enables reading or writing the selected internal register; never active together with DACK

pins.name: A0
pins.text: register address bit 0 (with CS)

pins.name: A1
pins.text: register address bit 1

pins.name: A2
pins.text: register address bit 2

pins.name: A3
pins.text: register address bit 3

pins.name: DACK
pins.text: data acknowledge: resets DREQ and selects the Data Register (the chip select for DMA transfers)

pins.name: TGS
pins.text: target group select: high when the chip works as target; enables the external REQ, MSG, C/D and I/O drivers

pins.name: DREQ
pins.text: data request in DMA mode: high when the Data Register has a byte for, or needs a byte from, the DMA; cleared by DACK

pins.name: WR
pins.text: write pulse: strobes the data bus into the selected internal register

pins.name: RD
pins.text: read pulse: puts the selected internal register on the data bus

pins.name: SELOUT
pins.text: high while the chip asserts SEL on the SCSI bus

pins.name: SBP
pins.text: SCSI data bus parity, active high, to the external transceivers; bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state)

pins.name: SB0
pins.text: SCSI data bus bit 0, active high, to the external SCSI bus transceivers; bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state)

behaviour.reason: A command-driven SCSI protocol controller (initiator and target roles, arbitration, selection and reselection, DMA and programmed transfers) run by internal state machines from a clock of up to 10 MHz. No 5386 data sheet was found, and the 5385E data sheet describes it in words, register tables and waveforms; a runnable pin model would be a full controller emulation. The words are in pins[].text.

note: No NCR 5386 data sheet (NCR MC-704) was found. Pin numbers and names are from NCR's own 5386 pinout drawing; what each pin does is from the 5385E data sheet. The 5386 differences (pass parity, valid phase enable, no extra DREQ) are in the notebook pages 4-5. Card 3207 sheet 19 matches the pinout on every pin used.
